title: War Bonds, Gravel, and Driveways in Austin
summary:
*   **Land Use and Infrastructure Debates:** The council considered a request from Janes Gravel Company and the International-Great Northern Railroad for additional land from the Sand Beach Reserve and a permanent street closure (Baylor Street) for a new railroad spur track, deferring action for further plans.
*   **Wartime Patriotism:** A unique permit was granted to the Women's Victory Committee to erect a small house on Congress Avenue for the specific purpose of selling War Bonds, highlighting local contributions to the war effort.
*   **Commercial Development Approved:** The U.S. Engineer Office, representing Travis County, received approval to construct commercial driveways for the Old Courthouse block, signaling ongoing urban development and federal agency involvement.
*   **Hospital Name Change Proposed:** A resolution from the Junior Chamber of Commerce recommending renaming the Travis County Tubercular Hospital to F. N. Moore Memorial Hospital was received and held for county review.

REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL:
Austin, Texas, March 18, 1943
The City Council convened in Regular Session, at the regular meeting place in the Council
Chamber at the Municipal Building, on Thursday, March 18, 1943, at 10:30 A. M., with the
following members present: Councilmen Alford, Bartholomew, and Gillis; absent, Mayor
Miller and Councilman Wolf. Mayor Pro Tem. Bartholomew presided over the meeting in the
absence of Mayor Miller.
There was present also: J. E. Mothoral, City Engineer.
The minutes of the Regular Meeting of March 11, 1943, were read; and upon motion of
Councilman Alford, were adopted as read by the following vote: "ayes," Councilmen Alford,
Bartholomew, and Gillis; "naya," none; Mayor Miller and Councilman Wolf absent.
Judge Ben H. Powell, Attorney for the International-Great Northern Railrond, and James D.
Parnell, representing the Janes Gravel Company, came before the Council in the matter of
certain improvements that said Company desires to build on property lying contiguous to
the Sand Beach Reserve, went of Lamar Boulevard; and, in this connection, requested: (1)
an additional three hundred feet of ground, being a part of the Sand Beach Reserve, in
addition to the strip of ground belonging to the City for which said Janes Gravel Company
has horetofore submitted an offer to purchase; and (2) the permanent closing of the south
end of Baylor Street, or, in lieu thereof, an easement across said street to said
Railroad for a spur track.
After considerable discussion, the matter was taken under advisement, pending submission
by petitioners of a complete sketch of the general plan for proposed improvements,
together with a definition of the kind of plant they intend to erect, for consideration by
the City Council, the Acting City Manager, and the City Engineer.
An appeal by E. S. Hinton on his application for a taxicab driver's permit, which had been
recommended for denial, was heard. Action on the matter was deferred to the next regular
meeting, ponding a further report from the Chief of Police on same.
The following resolution was offered by Councilman Gillis: (RESOLUTION) WHEREAS, The
County of Travis, acting by and through the U. S. Engineer Office, owner of what is known
as the Old Courthouse block, within the City of Austin, Travis County, Texas, which
property is situated between West 3rd Street and West 4th Street and San Antonio Strest
and Guadalupe Street, has made application to the City Council of the City of Austin for
permission to construct commercial driveways across the south sidewalk area of West 4th
Street and the east sidewalk area of San Antonio Street adjacent to the above described
property; and WHEREAS, A plan has been prepared showing the arrangement of said driveways,
which plan is hereto Attached marked 2-0-961, and made a part hereof; and WHEREAS, Said
request and plan have been reviewed and considered by the City Council of the City of
Austin; therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: THAT the
County of Travis, acting by and through the U. S. Engineer Office, owner of what is known
as the Old Courthouse block, within the City of Austin, Travis County, Texas, which
property is situated between West 3rd Street and West 4th Street, and San Antonio Street
and Guadalupe Street, is hereby permitted to construct commercial driveways across the
south sidewalk area of West 4th Street and the enst sidewalk area of San Antonio Street,
subject to the construction of concrete ramps, curbs, driveways, sidewalks, and expansion
joints, as shown upon the plan marked 2-0-961, which plan is hereto attached and made a
part of this resolution; and further subject to the condition that all concrete curb,
ramp, and driveway construction done at the above described location shall be done by the
U. S.
Engineer Office under the direction and supervision of the City Engineer of the City of
Austin, and in accordance with lines and grades furnished by the Engineering Department of
the City of Austin. 187
188
